Centre for Engineering Education Development
Centre for
Engineering Education Development 

KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology (KGRCET) has established the Centre for Engineering Education Development (CEED) with a strong commitment to advancing excellence and innovation in teaching–learning practices. Aligned with the institution’s vision of New Age Engineering, CEED serves as a strategic platform to empower faculty and enhance student learning through evidence-based, student-centric pedagogical approaches.

CEED works collaboratively with faculty members across departments to build capacity in modern teaching methodologies that promote active, experiential, and collaborative learning. Through a series of systematic and continuous faculty development initiatives, CEED enhances faculty awareness, competence, and confidence in implementing effective instructional practices grounded in educational research.

A key initiative of CEED is the Semester-Start Faculty Development Program, specially designed for newly joined faculty. This program emphasizes student-centered learning while also addressing essential aspects such as mentoring strategies, ethical teaching practices, classroom engagement, and effective classroom management. Throughout the semester, CEED conducts focused workshops and hands-on sessions on topics including Bloom’s Taxonomy, ICAP-based active learning strategies, assessment and evaluation principles, technology-enabled learning, Outcome-Based Education (OBE), and rubric design.

In addition to pedagogical training, CEED actively promotes the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL). The center supports faculty in documenting innovative classroom practices and conducting educational research by organizing paper review and discussion sessions that critically analyze engineering education journal articles. CEED members mentor faculty in preparing and publishing research papers in reputed engineering education conferences and journals at both national and international levels.

As a result of CEED’s sustained efforts, faculty at KGRCET have successfully transitioned from traditional lecture-based instruction to active, collaborative, and blended learning models. Several faculty members have developed course websites, digital resources, and technology-integrated instructional materials, enabling learning beyond the classroom and fostering deeper student engagement.

Through its comprehensive and impactful initiatives, CEED continues to play a pivotal role in enhancing teaching effectiveness, strengthening faculty professionalism, and ensuring the achievement of intended learning outcomes. CEED has also received national and international recognition for its significant contributions to engineering education, reinforcing KGRCET’s commitment to academic excellence and continuous improvement.

Teaching &
Learning Conclave

The Teaching and Learning Conclave organized by CEED is a platform where faculty showcase innovative, student-centric teaching methods aligned with Outcome-Based Education (OBE). Faculty members present evidence of active learning strategies and student reflections, which are evaluated by external experts from international teaching and learning centers to ensure quality and continuous improvement. The conclave nurtures reflective teaching practices and motivates adoption of effective pedagogical innovations. This regular conclave helps scale best practices across departments and strengthens culture of pedagogical excellence. Faculty presentations often drive improvements in classroom engagement and learning outcomes.

Faculty
Conclave Activities
Teachings &
Learning Seminars
Research
(CEED Focused)

CEED fosters educational research by supporting the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL), encouraging faculty to conduct classroom-based action research and investigate pedagogical innovations. It organizes programs like action-research work of extended duration, paper review sessions, and workshops that guide faculty in publishing research in reputed engineering education journals and conferences. CEED’s initiatives emphasize evidence-based practices, learning analytics, and reflective assessment to enhance teaching effectiveness. Through these activities, faculty engage deeply with research questions that improve students’ learning experiences. Educational research facilitated by CEED contributes to broader academic discussions in engineering pedagogy.

Awards and Achievements
in CEED

CEED has received national and international recognition for excellence in engineering education development, including the Outstanding Teaching and Learning Centre Award by IUCEE in 2023 and multiple teaching excellence awards in 2024. Leaders of CEED, such as Mrs. Tuti Sandhya and Mr. Khamruddin Syed, have been honored with leadership and reviewer recognitions at international education forums. Faculty associated with CEED have served as reviewers for prominent engineering education conferences and journals over many years. CEED team members have been certified and awarded for contributions to teaching and learning practices. These accolades reflect sustained impact in faculty development and evidence-based pedagogical innovation.

Capacity Building Programs -
CEED

1. Faculty Development on Student-Centered Teaching
This program focuses on transforming traditional lecture-based teaching into interactive, student-centered learning environments. Faculty members are trained in:

Active learning strategies such as think-pair-share, peer instruction, and collaborative learning
Flipped classroom methodologies
Classroom engagement techniques
Facilitating discussions and experiential learning
The program emphasizes shifting the focus from teacher delivery to student participation, thereby improving learning outcomes, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities.

2. Project & Problem-Based Learning (PBL) Implementation Workshops
CEED conducts specialized workshops to help faculty design and implement Project-Based and Problem-Based Learning models effectively. These workshops cover:

Designing real-world problem statements
Structuring PBL-based courses
Integrating interdisciplinary learning
Developing evaluation rubrics for projects
Monitoring and assessing student progress
Faculty learn how to guide students in solving practical engineering challenges, encouraging innovation, teamwork, and research orientation.

3. Technology-Enhanced Learning Programs
In response to the evolving digital education landscape, CEED organizes programs focused on technology integration in teaching. These include:

Blended learning models
Learning Management Systems (LMS) usage
Development of course websites
Creation of digital learning resources
Use of simulation tools and educational software
Online assessment techniques
These programs enhance faculty proficiency in leveraging technology to create flexible, accessible, and engaging learning environments.

4. Outcome-Based Education (OBE) and Assessment Training
CEED provides structured training on Outcome-Based Education principles to ensure alignment between curriculum, teaching, and assessment. The training includes:

Formulating Course Outcomes (COs) and Program Outcomes (POs)
CO-PO mapping strategies
Designing measurable learning outcomes
Developing effective assessment tools
Data analysis for continuous improvement
This initiative strengthens academic quality assurance and supports accreditation requirements by ensuring measurable and meaningful student achievement.

5. Action Research Programs
CEED encourages faculty to engage in pedagogical research through extended Action Research programs. These workshops guide faculty in:

Identifying classroom challenges
Designing research-based interventions
Collecting and analyzing educational data
Reflecting on teaching effectiveness
Publishing research in engineering education
This program promotes a culture of reflective practice and continuous improvement in teaching methodologies.

6. Bi-Monthly Reflection Meets & Teaching &Learning Conclaves 

To sustain collaborative learning and knowledge sharing, CEED organizes:
Bi-Monthly Reflection Meets

Faculty discussions on innovative practices
Sharing classroom experiences and challenges
Peer learning and mentoring
Feedback-driven improvements

These forums foster a vibrant academic community focused on excellence in engineering education.

Centre for Research Innovation & Development
Centre for Research
Innovations & Development

The Centre for Research Innovations & Development (CRID) is imperative for inclusive intellectual growth. It is often the first critical step in innovation and drives technological improvements which lead to Science and Technology (S&T) growth. KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology is continuously encouraging, supporting and promoting R&D activities by imparting training and workshops.

The institute is actively pursuing advanced research programs which are focused towards advancement of human knowledge and development of society. Research efforts are directed towards solving complex problems, delivering social benefits and driving economic prosperity, nationally as well as globally. The center (CRID) is responsible for the development and implementation of research strategy of the institute. It assists to formulate strategic planning for research and executing the plan. It co-ordinates academic management of the research of the institute as a whole, encourages faculty and departments to increase research grants from different funding organizations in India, and encourages national and international collaborations.

Vision

To become a centre of excellence recognized for fostering an ecosystem to promote research, innovation and development through strategic partnerships with academia, government organizations, and industries that will lead to the advancement of knowledge in STEM.

Mission
Encourage faculty, students, and research scholars to undertake research through independent and Ph.D.-driven projects, and publish outcomes in journals and conferences.
Collaborate with industries for consultancy projects and promote research leading to innovation and intellectual property creation.
Partner with government and non-government organizations on funded and independent projects to advance research and development.
Provide infrastructure, advanced research equipment, and capacity building to support innovation and R&D activities.
CRID
Goals
Encourage faculty, undergraduate, and postgraduate students to engage in research activities that inspire higher education and academic growth.
Facilitate seminars, workshops, and training programs to promote research, including awareness on intellectual property rights (IPR) and patent filing.
Support faculty and students in publishing research through assistance in writing, reviewing, and submitting papers to reputed journals and conferences.
Develop and implement structured guidelines for internal reviews to strengthen research progress and Ph.D. advancement.
Assist stakeholders in securing research funding through government and private sector schemes.
Collaborate with industries and organizations to co-develop innovative research solutions through mutual partnerships.
Objectives of
CRID

Research at KGRCET has been recognized as the primary activity to enhance teaching-learning process, and also to develop a unique identity as an institution that has committed itself to address societal issues through application of Science and Technology. The CRID division aims to continuously liaise with various funding agencies, R&D institutions, industries and faculty members of KGRCET to facilitate for undertaking innovative research in cutting-edge areas of application and social relevance.

Promote research and consultancy activities at the institutional level.
Facilitate collaboration with external agencies, including industries and government funding bodies.
Establish multiple thematic research areas to drive focused innovation.
Enhance the number of quality publications in refereed journals and conferences, along with intellectual property creation.
Support faculty and research scholars in preparing R&D proposals for external funding.
Encourage the development of innovative products and showcase them at national-level competitions.

Dean

Dr. L. Jayahari is a Professor of Mechanical Engineering with over 19 years of experience in teaching, research, and academic administration. He currently serves as Dean – Research & Development and has held key leadership positions including Dean Academics, Dean of Student Affairs, and Head of the Mechanical Engineering Department at reputed autonomous institutions in Hyderabad.

He holds a Ph.D. from JNTU Hyderabad, a Master’s degree from BTH, Sweden (with distinction), and a B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering. His research expertise lies in materials engineering, sheet metal forming, high- and sub-zero temperature forming, and advanced metal forming processes. He has published 30+ research papers in SCI and Scopus indexed journals and holds one published patent.

He has successfully secured sponsored research grants exceeding ₹29 lakhs from agencies such as AR&DB (DRDO), JNTUH-TEQIP, DST-SERB (Symposium Grant), and ATAL FDP (PI) Grant.

Dr. Jayahari has played a pivotal role in NBA and NAAC accreditations, contributing to NBA accreditation of multiple programs and the achievement of NAAC A++ grade at the institutional level. He has also established advanced research laboratories, guided 50+ UG and 15+ PG projects, and mentored doctoral scholars. His leadership continues to strengthen research culture, innovation, and outcome-based education in engineering institutions.

The Centre for Innovation and Social Transformation has a goal to help students contribute to socio-economic environmental growth in various communities. Encouraging innovative thinking and problem-solving skills, CIST gives students the opportunity to work with local community members, and identify their most pressing challenges. They then design and develop technology –based solutions, to improve the quality of living in these areas. Through capacity building and community- based learning programs, CIST aims to instill principles of Sustainable Development and United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG’s). Students involved in CIST activities are expected to emerge as leaders in the community, with a high sense of moral and civic responsibility towards the development of the country.

To become a centre of Excellence that fosters an ecosystem to promote engagement, innovation, and research leading to sustainable socio-economic development in the community.

Master of Business Administration

The Department of Master of Business Administration (MBA) at K G Reddy College of Engineering and Technology (KGRCET) is one of the prominent academic departments dedicated to nurturing future business leaders and management professionals. The department offers a two-year full-time postgraduate MBA programme, approved by AICTE and affiliated to JNTU Hyderabad, ensuring high academic standards and industry relevance.

The MBA programme is designed to develop students into competent, ethical, and dynamic managers capable of addressing the challenges of the modern business environment. The curriculum is structured into four semesters with an intake of approximately 60 students per batch, focusing on building managerial competence through a balanced blend of theoretical foundations and practical business applications.

The department adopts innovative teaching–learning practices that emphasize experiential and participative learning. Faculty members employ a variety of student-centric pedagogical approaches, including case study analysis, business simulations, role plays, group discussions, presentations, project-based learning, and problem-solving exercises. These methods help students develop analytical thinking, leadership abilities, strategic decision-making skills, and effective communication skills.

The MBA programme also encourages active student participation and collaborative learning, enabling students to explore management concepts from multidisciplinary perspectives. Regular seminars, workshops, guest lectures, industry interactions, and internships provide students with practical exposure and insights into contemporary business practices.

To strengthen managerial competencies, students are engaged in field research, industry-based projects, management games, quizzes, and presentations. The department promotes critical thinking, creativity, and innovation, preparing students to handle complex managerial situations and make informed business decisions.

The learning process is further supported through continuous and comprehensive evaluation, assessing students on various academic and professional parameters such as assignments, presentations, case analysis, projects, and semester examinations.

The Department also organizes state-level management fests, academic seminars, and co-curricular activities, which enhance students’ leadership, teamwork, and organizational skills. These activities help students gain confidence and develop a holistic personality required for professional success.

The department is supported by a team of highly qualified, experienced, and committed faculty members who play a crucial role in mentoring students and fostering a culture of academic excellence, professional ethics, and lifelong learning.

	
Vision

To be recognized as a leading program that develops the future leaders by fostering a learning culture cantered around innovative teaching, research, entrepreneurship and community engagement.

	
Mission
To offer an industry-aligned curriculum through innovative teaching learning practices to prepare students for a career in diverse fields.
To provide an ecosystem and opportunities for students and faculty to engage in innovation, research and entrepreneurship.
To foster an environment for holistic learning and development that allows the students to become socially responsible business leaders.

Mechanical Engineering

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology was established in 2009 and offers a four-year undergraduate program in Mechanical Engineering. Committed to academic excellence, the department implements innovative teaching-learning practices (TL-P) to ensure the effective delivery of Outcome-Based Education (OBE). This commitment has led to the department’s accreditation for three years (from 30-05- 2024 to 30-06-2027) under the TIER II format, applicable to students graduating between 2024 and 2027.

Mechanical Engineering is a highly versatile discipline that influences various aspects of daily life and industry. The department's strength lies in its dedicated faculty, skilled technical staff, and enthusiastic students. The Board of Studies continuously updates the curriculum to align with industry advancements and emerging technologies. The program equips future engineers with modern engineering tools and a strong foundation in the principles of force, motion, and energy, enabling them to develop innovative solutions to complex engineering challenges across diverse industries.

The Department is equipped with state-of-the-art laboratories that provide students with hands-on learning experiences. With funding support from DST, a dedicated research laboratory has been established, featuring advanced equipment such as a CNC Router, CNC Fiber Laser Cutting Machine, 1500W 3-in-1 Fiber Laser Welding Machine, and an NC Sheet Metal Bending Machine, Co2 Laser cut CNC Machine, Milling machine. From the first year onward, the curriculum emphasizes both conventional drawing techniques and computer-aided engineering graphics, fostering strong design skills. The department houses 14 well-equipped laboratories along with an Emerging Technology Club, specializing in 3D printing. Through certification courses, students receive training in various modeling and analysis software, enabling them to undertake mini and major projects using in-house laboratory facilities.The Emerging Technology Club actively encourages student participation in interinstitute competitions, leading to significant achievements at state and national levels, further strengthening their technical expertise and innovation skills.

The department maintains strong industry partnerships, ensuring alignment with evolving industry needs through active contributions to curriculum design, industrial visits, expert lectures, and workshops. These collaborations enable students to gain practical exposure and hands-on experience in their respective fields. We have established partnerships with leading organizations such as Automated Tooling Systems Pvt. Ltd, Government Technical Tool Room (Karnataka), Design Labs, H-Bots Robotics, ESCI, IIIT Hyderabad, GRIET, Samskriti Foundation, and BVIC – NGO, among others. These collaborations provide students with valuable internship opportunities in manufacturing, design, and thermal specializations. Additionally, industry visits allow students to engage with real-world challenges, fostering innovation and problem-solving skills. Furthermore, our partnerships with NGOs enable students to contribute to social issues, promoting sustainable development. As a result of these initiatives, 24 students from the 2021-25 graduating batch have secured stipend-based internships, with compensation ranging from ₹7,000 to ₹15,000, reinforcing the department’s commitment to industry-oriented learning and professional growth.
The department, in collaboration with the institute, has established a transparent appraisal system aimed at fostering both institutional and faculty development. This system emphasizes key areas such as academics, research, professional growth, and service to the institution. Faculty members are encouraged to set personal and professional goals, with dedicated research hours provided each week to support their scholarly pursuits. To further incentivize excellence, faculty members receive performance-based increments for achievements such as publishing research papers, filing patents, and contributing to book chapters. As a result of this structured approach, the department has successfully produced 14 SCI-indexed papers, 78 Scopus-indexed conference papers, and filed 5 patents, with 2 already granted. Additionally, undergraduate student projects have led to 18 publications and 3 published patents, showcasing the department's commitment to academic and research excellence.

	
Vision

To be recognized as a department, providing quality technical education and producing highly competent and skilled engineers to suit the latest trends in modern industry and to act as a catalyst for sustainable development.

	
Mission
To impart quality education to the students and enhance their skills by integrating strong fundamentals, practical skills through Curriculum, and industry interaction, enabling graduates to contribute effectively to engineering practice.
To integrate innovative teaching and learning practices that enables students to build strong technical competence in mechanical Engineering
To foster a collaborative environment that encourages innovation, research and Entrepreneurship among faculty and students, contributing to sustainable development.

Computer Science & Engineering Data Science

B.Tech in Data science continues to evolve as one of the most promising and in-demand career paths for skilled professionals. Today, successful data professionals understand that they must advance past the traditional skills of analyzing large amounts of data, data mining, and programming skills. In order to uncover useful intelligence for their organizations, data scientists must master the full spectrum of the data science life cycle and possess a level of flexibility and understanding to maximize returns at each phase of the process.

In the past decade, data scientists have become necessary assets and are present in almost all organizations. These professionals are well-rounded, data-driven individuals with high-level technical skills who are capable of building complex quantitative algorithms to organize and synthesize large amounts of information used to answer questions and drive strategy in their organization. This is coupled with the experience in communication and leadership needed to deliver tangible results to various stakeholders across an organization or business.

Data scientists need to be curious and result-oriented, with exceptional industry-specific knowledge and communication skills that allow them to explain highly technical results to their non-technical counterparts. They possess a strong quantitative background in statistics and linear algebra as well as programming knowledge with focuses in data warehousing, mining, and modeling to build and analyze algorithms.

They must also be able to utilize key technical tools and skills, including:

Computer Science & Engineering

Computer Science and Engineering stands as one of the most dynamic and rapidly evolving disciplines of the modern era. Within a relatively short span of time, it has emerged as a cornerstone of global innovation, driving technological advancement across industries. Pursuing a career in Computer Science and Engineering has proven to be a highly rewarding pathway for aspiring professionals, and the future of this domain continues to shine with immense promise in the digital millennium.

Established in 2008 with an initial intake of 60 students, the Department of Computer Science and Engineering has witnessed remarkable growth, expanding its intake to 300 students in the academic year 2024–25. This progression reflects the department’s academic excellence, growing reputation, and commitment to meeting the evolving demands of the technology-driven world.

The department is distinguished by a team of highly qualified, experienced, and dedicated faculty committed to fostering the holistic development of students. Notably, the department is strengthened by eight doctoral faculty members, whose scholarly expertise and research orientation enrich the academic environment and promote a culture of intellectual inquiry.

Equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure, the department provides an advanced learning ecosystem that nurtures innovation and technical mastery. Students benefit from access to high-performance computing systems, modern servers, well-stocked libraries with the latest titles, NPTEL courseware, scholarly journals, and high-bandwidth internet connectivity, ensuring an immersive and effective educational experience.

To prepare students for the challenges of a competitive global landscape, the department emphasizes exposure to emerging technology through seminars, workshops, guest lectures, and technical symposiums. Participation in paper presentations, technical contests, and a wide spectrum of co-curricular and extracurricular activities further enhances professional competencies. A robust mentoring framework ensures continuous monitoring of student progress while supporting personality development, leadership qualities, and career readiness.

Through its unwavering commitment to academic rigor, innovation, and student success, the Department of Computer Science and Engineering continues to shape future-ready professionals equipped to excel in academia, research, and the ever-expanding technology industry.

	
Vision

To be recognized as a department of excellence by stimulating a learning environment in which students and faculty will thrive and grow to achieve their professional, institutional, entrepreneurial and societal goals.

	
Mission
To provide high quality technical education to students that will enable life-long learning and build expertise in advanced technologies in Computer Science and Engineering.
To promote research and development by providing opportunities to solve complex engineering problems in collaboration with industry and government agencies.
To encourage professional development of students that will inculcate ethical values and leadership skills through entrepreneurship while working with the community to address societal issues.

Institution Industry Collaboration 
IIC
 

The Institute-Industry Collaboration (IIC) at KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology serves as a strategic bridge between academia and industry, ensuring that education remains relevant, practical, and future-ready. Through partnerships with leading organizations, curriculum enrichment, expert interactions, collaborative research, consultancy services, industrial visits, and skill development programs, IIC fosters innovation and real-world exposure for both students and faculty. By aligning academic practices with evolving industry demands, KGRCET cultivates competent engineering professionals equipped to thrive in a rapidly advancing technological landscape.

Admission Enquiry
Functions & 
Responsibilities
 
Functions & Responsibilities of the Industry-Institute Collaboration (IIC):
Designing educational programs aligned with industry demands to cultivate engineering professionals capable of navigating rapid technological advancements.
Providing resources for continuous learning and skill enhancement for engineers and technologists to meet the evolving needs of the industry.
Establishing an Industry-Institute partnership and fostering interaction between the two sectors.
Hosting workshops, conferences, and symposia jointly attended by faculty and industry representatives.
Inviting industry professionals to deliver lectures at the institution, enriching the learning experience for students.
Facilitating the involvement of industry experts in curriculum development, ensuring relevance and applicability.
Organizing visits for faculty members to various industries, fostering understanding and collaboration.
Offering professional consultancy services to industries by the faculty.
Conducting industrial testing, either on-site or in laboratories, to provide valuable insights and solutions.
Undertaking collaborative research programs and field studies involving faculty and industry personnel.
Establishing Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) between the institute and industries to formalize collaboration efforts.
Developing human resource through tailored programs designed by faculty for practicing engineers, enhancing their skills and knowledge base.

Unnat Bharat Abhiyan
About 
Unnat Bharat Abhiyan
 

The conceptualization of Unnat Bharat Abhiyan started with the initiative of a group of dedicated faculty members of Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi working for long in the area of rural development and appropriate technology. The concept was nurtured through wide consultation with the representatives of a number of technical institutions, Rural Technology Action Group (RuTAG) coordinators, voluntary organizations and government agencies, actively involved in rural development work, during a National workshop held at IIT Delhi in September, 2014. The workshop was sponsored by Council for Advancement of People’s Action and Rural Technology (CAPART), Ministry of Rural Development, Govt. of India. The program was formally launched by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) in presence of The President of India on 11th November, 2014.

Vision

Unnat Bharat Abhiyan is inspired by the vision of transformational change in rural development processes by leveraging knowledge institutions to help build the architecture of an Inclusive India.

Mission

The Mission of Unnat Bharat Abhiyan is to enable higher educational institutions to work with the people of rural India in identifying development challenges and evolving appropriate solutions for accelerating sustainable growth. It also aims to create a virtuous cycle between society and an inclusive academic system by providing knowledge and practices for emerging professions and to upgrade the capabilities of both the public and the private sectors in responding to the development needs of rural India.

About 
Department
 

The department of Humanities & Sciences (H&S) is established in the year 2008 in KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology (KGRCET). This department offers a strong foundation for the Engineering Education by the dissemination of the requisite knowledge both in Basic sciences and Humanities through various innovative and active teaching learning methods, tutorials, make up and remedial classes. We do extend one to one and group mentoring to the students. The students are exposed to various activities through the clubs to ensure their holistic development. The H&S department includes the departments of English,  Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. The department has well qualified (Doctorate and Post doc) and experienced (5 years- 36 years) faculties to deliver the best to the aspiring students. In addition to the teaching of English as a course, we have a Public speaking club that inculcates confidence, develop communication skills and personality traits and groom our students as excellent communicators and global leaders. The department has well equipped language laboratories and well-trained faculty members who can guide the students to learn and curate their language quotient to the requirements of job market. Mathematics is the queen of sciences and technology while Physics is the language of Engineers. Without the application of Mathematics no complex Engineering problems can be solved. Department has a Computational Mathematics lab and helps the students to solve numerical equations using Mathlab. To solve the mysteries of nature, Physics plays a prominent role and the engineers use this physics as a language for finding solutions to many engineering problems.We have well equipped labs to train the students on the basics applications. Both well-equipped laboratory and expert faculties are crucial to deliver the subject and to make the learning enjoyable. The study of Chemistry is essential to understand the chemical reactions in all the manufacturing process. Our chemistry department has both well- equipped labs and expert faculties. In short, the department of humanities and sciences plays a key role in churning out the future change makers and engineer strong technocrats.

Our Vision
To establish a strong foundation in basic sciences such as Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, which in turn help the students to excel in their core engineering discipline and also train them to acquire proficiency in English language communication.
Our Mission
To provide academic excellence in basic sciences in the perspective of engineering.
Students and faculties are provided learning environment where they can master in engineering discipline by applying knowledge from basic sciences.
Inculcate research culture through project based assignments.
Program Outcomes
PO I: Engineering knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO II: Problem analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.
PO III: Design/development of solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental
considerations.
PO IV: Conduct investigations of complex problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.
PO V: Modern tool usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.
PO VI: The engineer and society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.
PO VII: Environment and sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of and need for sustainable development.
PO VIII: Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
PO IX: Individual and team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.
PO X: Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.
PO XI: Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO XII: Life-long learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

Research

KGRCET supports research among the faculties and students. For this purpose we have established a Center for Research Innovation and Development (CRID) headed by the Dean Research , assisted by associate Dean Research and CRID coordinators from each department. We have designated research labs in each department labs to promote research activities. A well matured research policy is envisaged for this purpose the CRID conducts FDP’s Workshop’s awareness programs etc. on research and every care is taken to maintain quality and ethics among the faculties and the students. The college encourages the faculties to publish quality papers in Scopus, web of science and SCI journals  every support is provided to the faculty to publish papers, to attend conferences etc. The institute provides opportunities to the faculties to collaborate with other institutes and leading institutions.

Value Added Courses

With the sole aim of developing socially conscious individuals at local, regional and national level by inculcating a sense of social responsibility we have established the Centre for Innovation and Social Transformation (CIST). During the Academic year we have conducted 2 courses as value added courses for the first year and in the AY 2023-24, we continue to offer the same courses Design Thinking and Sustainable Development (DTSD) and Social Innovation (SI) to the first year students as credit courses for value addition. Through these we have Initiated village visits and had interaction with the village elders and understood their problems, defined the problem, pitching, analysis, arriving at solutions, prototyping and finally product development. They provide cost effective and affordable solutions to literacy promotion, hygiene, health care, education and agriculture.

Best Practices

We provide the additional learning materials like question bank, hand written notes, recorded videos and university question papers with solutions and utilize the tutorial classes to clarify the student doubts if any in various courses. Also we conduct revision classes for difficult topics in different courses which helps them to prepare well for the mid and semester end examination. As a part of the Continuous Internal Evaluation in each course the students are to give presentations on the topics listed by the concerned faculty. This also helps them to learn the topics, gain confidence and develop communication skills.

The advanced learners are encouraged to do the certification courses along with their regular course work. The college offers 8 certification courses in the first year. The students are also encouraged to participate in project based learning, hackathons, online courses and internships.

(NSS)
 

The main aim of conducting National Service Scheme program in KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology is to create Personality Development through Community Service. This program is to motivate and encourage, the social welfare thoughts in the students and to provide service to the society without any prejudice. NSS volunteers are dedicated to this work to ensure that every one in our society who is needy gets every possible help from them so that they can also enhance their standards and lead a life of dignity in the society with all of us. In doing so the volunteers themselves learn a lot like how to struggle and how to lead a happy life in the extreme scarcity of resources and so on.

The main objectives of NSS are:

Understand the community in which they work.
Understand themselves in relation to their community.
Identify the needs and problems of the community and involve them in problem-solving.
Develop among themselves a sense of social and civic responsibility.
Utilize their knowledge in finding practical solutions to individual and community problems.
Develop competence required for group-living and sharing of responsibilities.
Gain skills in mobilizing community participation.
Acquire leadership qualities and democratic attitudes.
Develop capacity to meet emergencies and natural disasters and Practice national integration and social harmony

Motto:
The Motto of NSS "Not Me But You", reflects the essence of democratic living and upholds the need for self-less service. NSS helps the students develop appreciation to other person's point of view and also show consideration for fellow human beings. The philosophy of the NSS is well doctrine in this motto, which underlines/on the belief that the welfare of an individual is ultimately dependent on the welfare of the society on the whole and therefore, the NSS volunteers shall strive for the well-being of the society.

Symbol:
The symbol for the NSS has been based on the giant Rath Wheel of the world famous Konark Sun Temple (The Black Pagoda) situated in Orissa, India. The wheel portrays the cycle of creation, preservation and release and signifies the movement in life across time and space. The symbol thus stands for continuity as well as change and implies the continuous striving of NSS for social change.

Badge:
The NSS Symbol is embossed on the badge. The eight bars in the wheel represent the 24 hours of a day. The red colour indicates that the volunteer is full of young blood that is lively, active, energetic and full of high spirit. The navy blue colour indicates the cosmos of which the NSS is tiny part, ready to contribute its share for the welfare of the mankind.

NSS DAY:
NSS was formally launched on 24th September 1969, the birth centenary year of the Father of the Nation. Therefore, 24 September is celebrated every year as NSS Day with appropriate programmes and activities.

NSS Song:
During Silver Jubilee Year the NSS theme song has been composed. All NSS volunteers are expected to learn the theme song and sing the song during NSS events.

Policies and Guidelines
Policies and 
Guidelines
 

Placement Policy:

Students who are placed in a company with a package below 2.5 LPA will be permitted to participate in placement drives only for companies offering an annual package of 5 LPA and above.
Students who are placed in a company with a package between 3 LPA and 4 LPA will be permitted to participate in placement drives only for companies offering an annual package of 5 LPA and above.
If any company offers a package of 5 LPA or higher, all candidates—whether placed or unplaced—will be permitted to participate in the campus recruitment drive.
It is mandatory for all eligible students (including those who have already secured placements) to participate in on-campus recruitment drives.
Blacklisted students will be allowed to participate in placement drives only with special permission from the Faculty In-Charge, Training & Placement.
If any candidate submits willingness to participate in a placement drive (on-campus or off-campus) but fails to attend the Pre-Placement Talk (PPT), company-specific training, or CRT program, they may be blacklisted from Training & Placement.
If a candidate is blacklisted from the Training & Placement Cell, they will not be allowed to participate in any placement drives throughout the academic year.

Code of Conduct:

Only Training & Placement student coordinators have the authority to handle Training & Placement matters (internal or external).
Other students may handle such matters only with special permission from the Head of the Department (HOD).
All communication between students and companies after receiving a job offer must be routed through the Placement Cell.
Direct communication with company officials is not allowed.
Students must register to participate in the placement process of a company.
Attendance in Pre-Placement Talks (PPT) and CRT programs is mandatory after registration to be eligible for further placement processes.
Any misbehavior or complaints reported by company officials will be taken seriously. If proven, the student will be debarred from future placements or blacklisted.

Placement Guidelines:

The Training & Placement (T&P) Cell acts as a facilitator for placement-related activities and does not guarantee jobs.
Placement opportunities are provided under the policy of “One Job to One Student at the First Instance” to ensure fair distribution of opportunities.
All students must possess a PAN Card and Aadhaar Card and produce them when required by the company or T&P Cell.
In case of immediate joining, the college will issue a No Objection Certificate (NOC) and provide attendance support.
A candidate will be blacklisted if they express willingness to participate in a placement drive but fail to attend on the scheduled day.

Mrs. Ch Chandana
MCA, MBA, (Ph.D)
Assistant Professor, HOD - MBA
hod.mba@kgr.ac.in

Biography
Mrs. Ch. Chandana is the Head of the Department of MBA and HR Head at KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology. She brings around 10 years of combined teaching and industry experience, blending academic expertise with practical organizational exposure. With a strong interdisciplinary background in Computer Science, Computer Applications, and Management, she is committed to strengthening management education through outcome-based learning and industry-relevant practices.

Her professional journey integrates academic leadership with real-world industry insights, enabling her to bridge the gap between theoretical concepts and managerial application. As an academic administrator, she actively contributes to curriculum enrichment, faculty development, student mentoring, and industry–institute collaboration initiatives. She is particularly dedicated to empowering students from diverse and rural educational backgrounds by building their confidence, self-efficacy, and professional competence.

Research Interests
Mrs. Ch. Chandana’s research interests focus on Human Resource Management, Performance Management Systems, and data-driven decision-making in higher education institutions. Her primary research area is “Predicting Employee Retention in Indian Higher Educational Institutions Using Artificial Intelligence: The Mediating Role of Organizational Culture and Employee Engagement.” This research integrates AI-based predictive analytics with organizational culture and employee engagement frameworks to examine workforce retention patterns and institutional sustainability. Her work emphasizes performance analysis, competency alignment, appraisal systems, and strategic HR interventions that enhance long-term organizational effectiveness in academic institutions.

In addition, she actively undertakes action research in management education, particularly focusing on rural MBA students and their active participation and learning outcomes. Her research examines the role of self-efficacy, expectancy-value beliefs, and structured pedagogical interventions in improving classroom engagement, confidence, and managerial competency development. Through evidence-based teaching–learning models, she contributes to inclusive academic practices, performance-oriented management education, and continuous improvement in professional postgraduate programs.

Teaching–Learning Philosophy
Mrs. Chandana strongly believes that MBA education must be interactive, experiential, and competency-driven. Her teaching methodology emphasizes case-based discussions, real-time business problem analysis, role plays, simulations, management games, and student-led presentations to promote active participation and critical thinking. She integrates industry expert sessions, live projects, and continuous formative assessment to ensure measurable student outputs and learning outcomes.

Her classroom approach is centered on building self-efficacy, communication skills, analytical ability, and leadership qualities among MBA students. By creating an inclusive and engaging academic environment, she ensures that students not only gain theoretical knowledge but also develop practical managerial capabilities and employability skills aligned with industry expectations.

Dr. Angotu Saida
M.Tech, Ph. D
Professor, HOD ECE
hod.ece@kgr.ac.in

Biography
Dr. Angotu Saida is an accomplished academician and researcher with over 15 years of teaching experience in the field of Electronics and Communication Engineering. He obtained his B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering from SRTIST, Nalgonda, and completed his M.Tech in ECE from MITS, Kodad, Telangana. He was awarded his Ph.D. in Electronics and Communication Engineering from Bhagwant University, Ajmer, Rajasthan in 2024, with a research focus on MIMO-Based LTE-Advanced Antenna Design for 5G Communication.

Currently, Dr. Saida serves as an Associate Professor and Head of the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering at KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology, Hyderabad. Throughout his career, he has actively contributed to teaching, research, accreditation activities (NBA/NAAC), academic leadership, and examination administration, demonstrating a strong commitment to outcome-based education and academic excellence.

Research Interests
Dr. Saida’s research interests are primarily theoretical and analytical, aligned with core Electronics and Communication Engineering domains. His areas of interest include Electromagnetic Field Theory, Transmission Line Theory, Antenna Theory and Radiation Analysis, Microwave Engineering, and Wave Propagation. He also works on Wireless Communication and MIMO System Theory, Digital Communication and Coding Theory, and Internet of Things and it’s applications. His research focuses on strengthening theoretical foundations and applying analytical models to emerging communication systems such as LTE-Advanced and 5G networks, with emphasis on performance analysis and system optimization.

Teaching Interests
Dr. Saida is deeply committed to teaching both undergraduate and postgraduate students in core and advanced subjects of Electronics and Communication Engineering. His teaching interests include Electromagnetic Theory and Transmission Lines, Antennas and Wave Propagation, Microwave Engineering, Analog and Digital Communication, Probability Theory and Stochastic Processing, Electronic circuit Analysis, Pulse and Digital Circuits, and VLSI System Design. He emphasizes conceptual clarity, analytical thinking, and outcome-based education, and actively integrates theory with practical applications to enhance student learning.

Publications
Dr. Angotu Saida has published more than 25 research papers in reputed international journals and conferences, including IEEE, Springer, AIP Conference Proceedings, E3S, and MATEC Web of Conferences. His research publications cover areas such as 5G and MIMO antenna systems, VLSI architectures, wireless communication, IoT-based systems, and embedded technologies. He also serves as a reviewer for reputed international journals and IEEE co-sponsored conferences.

Awards & Honors
Dr. Saida has received several professional recognitions for his academic and research contributions. He received the Best Author Award for a book published by Alpha International Publication. He has been recognized as a Reviewer for reputed international journals and IEEE co-sponsored conferences, and served as a Session Chair for ICICACS-2025. He has also played a significant role in NBA accreditation (3-year accreditation) and NAAC-related academic quality initiatives.

DSA Orientation & Student Clubs Membership Drive for First-Year Students

Aug 25, 2026 | Events | 0 comments

The Department of Student Affairs (DSA) at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology organized a comprehensive orientation program for first-year students to welcome them into the college community and help them begin their academic journey with confidence.

The orientation introduced students to the institution’s vision, values, academic support systems, and the wide range of co-curricular and extracurricular opportunities available on campus. Students were also familiarized with various student clubs and community service initiatives, including the National Service Scheme (NSS), KGR Cares, Engineers Without Borders (EWB), and Street Cause.

The session emphasized the importance of active participation beyond the classroom, highlighting how these platforms help students develop confidence, leadership, communication, teamwork, and social responsibility.

The Head of the Department of Student Affairs, Mr. M. Rathna Chary, addressed the gathering with an inspiring message. He emphasized the role of DSA in supporting and guiding students throughout their college journey and encouraged the freshers to embrace new challenges, explore their talents, and make the most of the opportunities available to them.

Student Clubs Membership Drive

As part of the student engagement initiatives, the Department of Student Affairs also organized a vibrant Student Clubs Membership Drive exclusively for first-year students. The initiative aimed to introduce students to the diverse clubs and societies on campus and encourage them to actively participate in campus life.

During the drive, students were introduced to various technical societies, cultural associations, literary forums, sports clubs, and community service groups, including NSS. Faculty coordinators and senior student leaders explained the objectives and activities of the clubs while highlighting how participation can strengthen creativity, leadership, teamwork, communication, and professional skills.

The membership drive witnessed enthusiastic participation from the first-year students, who showed keen interest in exploring new areas, discovering their talents, connecting with peers, and contributing to the college community.

Together, the DSA Orientation and Student Clubs Membership Drive provided first-year students with a strong foundation for an engaging and enriching college experience. The initiatives reflected KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology’s commitment to holistic student development, active campus engagement, leadership, and responsible citizenship.

Strategic Advancement in Cloud Computing and DevOps Integration

Mar 17, 2026 | CSE

This technical workshop represents more than just a training session; it serves as a bridge between theoretical classroom concepts and the high-stakes reality of modern IT operations. By partnering with Teks Academy, the department provided students with a rare opportunity to learn directly from a Cloud Architect whose 15-year tenure spans multiple industries. This depth of experience offered participants a nuanced understanding of how global enterprises navigate digital transformation. Instead of focusing solely on isolated tools, the workshop emphasized a holistic view of the software development lifecycle, demonstrating how Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automated CI/CD pipelines are no longer optional but foundational to contemporary engineering roles.

The inclusion of Generative AI within the cloud ecosystem discussions was particularly forward-thinking, addressing the rapid shift toward AI-integrated operations (AIOps). Students explored how cloud platforms provide the necessary muscle for Large Language Models and how DevOps practices ensure these sophisticated tools can be deployed reliably and at scale. By examining the intersection of these technologies, the App & Web Development Club has effectively widened the professional horizon for its members, preparing them to enter a workforce where the ability to manage intelligent, scalable systems is the primary measure of technical proficiency.

Furthermore, this initiative underscores a strategic commitment to student employability and institutional excellence. By facilitating direct interaction with industry veterans, the computer science & engineering department ensures that its future graduates are not just "job-ready" in name, but possess the practical confidence to tackle real-world architectural challenges. The success of this collaboration sets a high bar for future academic endeavors, proving that when the department aligns its curriculum with the pulse of the industry, it creates a powerful environment for innovation. Moving forward, these insights into operational excellence and scalable infrastructure will likely serve as the cornerstone for many students' senior projects and professional careers.

Hands-On Experiential Learning and Hardware Interfacing

Feb 24, 2026 | CSE

While the theoretical foundations of computer science and electrical engineering provide the "why," practical laboratory sessions are where students discover the "how." Transitioning from a sanitized, virtual IDE to a breadboard teeming with jumper wires and integrated circuits represents a significant shift in a learner's cognitive development. In this physical environment, code is no longer just an abstract sequence of logic; it becomes a series of electrical impulses—high and low voltage states—that must interact precisely with the physical properties of transistors, capacitors, and resistors.

This transition introduces students to the gritty reality of hardware debugging, a discipline far removed from simply checking for syntax errors. In a lab setting, a program might fail not because of a logical flaw, but because of "noise" in a signal, a loose ground wire, or the thermal limitations of a component. By engaging directly with sensor modules—such as accelerometers, ultrasonic transducers, or infrared receivers—students learn to navigate the complexities of the physical world, including signal attenuation and environmental interference. They begin to appreciate the necessity of low-level drivers and the intricacies of communication protocols like $I^2C$, $SPI$, and $UART$.

Furthermore, these sessions foster a unique form of technical agility. When a system fails in a laboratory, the solution often requires a holistic approach that bridges the gap between domains. A student might need to use an oscilloscope to visualize a pulse-width modulation ($PWM$) signal to understand why a motor isn't spinning at the commanded speed, effectively diagnosing a software timing issue through physical observation. This cross-disciplinary troubleshooting is essential for designing modern integrated systems, such as robotics or IoT devices, where the software and hardware are inextricably linked.

Ultimately, the collaborative nature of the lab environment mirrors professional engineering settings. Students must communicate technical hurdles, share diagnostic tools, and iterate on designs in real-time. This hands-on experience demystifies the "black box" of technology, transforming students from mere consumers of high-level languages into architects who understand the fundamental physics that power their code.

Distinguished Guests from CSI Leadership

The Computer Society of India is organized into Regions and Chapters. For a Hyderabad-based college, the guests often include members of the CSI Hyderabad Chapter or the CSI Region V (which covers Telangana and Andhra Pradesh) leadership.

Chief Guest/Guest of Honor: Often, this is the Chairman of the CSI Hyderabad Chapter or a Regional Vice President. Industry Experts and Keynote Speakers

To provide students with a real-world perspective, colleges often invite a Chief Guest from the IT industry. This might be a Project Manager, Director, or CTO from nearby tech hubs like HITEC City or Gachibowli.

Role: These guests focus on "Bridging the Gap between Academia and Industry." They discuss emerging trends like AI, Cybersecurity, and Cloud Computing, emphasizing how CSI membership helps in networking and professional growth.
Ceremony Highlights

The event generally follows a formal protocol: the Lighting of the Lamp, the unveiling of the CSI Logo/Charter, and the Badging Ceremony where student office bearers (President, Vice-President, Secretary) are officially recognized. Hands-on Workshop on Blockchain Technology

Jan 31, 2026 | CSE

The hands-on workshop on Blockchain Technology, organized specifically for III-year students in collaboration with the Blockchain Club, served as a transformative educational milestone, bridging the gap between abstract cryptographic theories and tangible digital innovation. In an era where decentralized ledgers are redefining global industries, this initiative provided students with a comprehensive roadmap to navigate the complexities of Web3. The curriculum was meticulously designed to transition from high-level architectural overviews to granular, code-based execution, ensuring that every participant emerged with a functional understanding of how decentralized systems operate in a live environment.

The foundational phase of the workshop focused on the core pillars of blockchain: decentralization, immutability, and consensus mechanisms. Students explored the structural logic of blocks, hashes, and the distributed ledger technology that underpins modern cryptocurrencies and enterprise solutions. To solidify these concepts, the session transitioned into a practical exploration of the Remix IDE, a powerful web-based tool that allows developers to write, compile, and deploy code. This exposure was crucial, as it allowed students to visualize the blockchain environment and understand how transactions are validated and recorded within a simulated network.

On the second day, the intensity of the workshop escalated as students delved into the world of Smart Contracts using the Solidity programming language. This segment was particularly impactful, as it empowered students to write self-executing scripts that automate complex agreements without the need for intermediaries. By participating in Pre-Ikarus training, the cohort gained rare, practical insights into real-world blockchain workflows, learning how to troubleshoot deployment errors and optimize gas fees. This rigorous training ensured that the students weren't just observers of the technology but were active creators within the ecosystem.

The success of this intensive program was made possible through the unwavering support and visionary leadership of the Principal, Vice Principal, and the Head of the Department (CSE). Their commitment to integrating cutting-edge technology into the academic framework provided the necessary resources and motivation for the event. Furthermore, the seamless coordination between the organizing faculty and the energetic members of the Blockchain Club ensured a high-energy learning atmosphere. By the conclusion of the workshop, the students had not only enhanced their technical portfolios but also cultivated a forward-thinking mindset, positioning themselves as competitive candidates in the rapidly evolving landscape of software development and financial technology.

Hands-on Workshop on Prompt Engineering & Freelancing :

Jan 31, 2026 | CSE

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), in collaboration with the App & Web Development Club, recently orchestrated a transformative hands-on workshop dedicated to the cutting-edge domains of Prompt Engineering and Freelancing. Specifically designed for second-year students, the event aimed to bridge the gap between traditional academic curricula and the rapidly evolving landscape of contemporary AI-assisted development. As the industry shifts toward "AI-first" workflows, this workshop provided a vital platform for students to transition from passive consumers of technology to active, efficient architects of digital solutions.

The morning session was dedicated to the foundational principles of Prompt Engineering. Rather than viewing AI as a simple "search box," students were taught to treat Large Language Models (LLMs) as sophisticated collaborators. The curriculum focused on the nuances of context setting, role prompting, and iterative refinement. By understanding the underlying logic of how AI processes instructions, students learned how to craft precise queries that minimize hallucinations and maximize high-quality output for real-world applications. This segment emphasized that the future of engineering lies not just in writing code, but in the logical articulation of problems and the strategic direction of autonomous agents.

Following the theoretical foundation of the morning, the afternoon session transitioned into an exhilarating live demonstration of "vibe coding." This modern paradigm shifts the developer's focus from syntax-heavy manual entry to high-level conceptualization, where natural language serves as the primary interface for building complex software. Through interactive activities, students witnessed firsthand how ideas could be translated into functional prototypes in minutes. This session was particularly impactful as it demystified the barrier to entry for software development, highlighting that logical thinking and creative problem-solving are the most valuable assets a developer possesses in the age of generative AI.

The workshop also addressed the professional side of these skills through a deep dive into the world of Freelancing. By mastering prompt engineering and vibe coding, students were shown how they could leverage their increased productivity to secure global opportunities on platforms like Upwork and GitHub. This holistic approach ensured that participants left not only with technical proficiency but also with a clear roadmap for financial independence and career growth. By fostering an environment of innovation and practical learning, the CSE Department has successfully empowered the next generation of engineers to lead in an AI-driven economy

By stepping outside the traditional classroom environment, our students were immersed in an atmosphere of collaborative engineering, where the focus shifted from theoretical calculations to the practical, human-centric application of technology. The event served as a rigorous training ground for the next generation of engineers, emphasizing that the true value of technical skill lies in its ability to solve pressing societal issues.

IUCEE–NEP course , Quantum Computing

Jan 21, 2026 | CSE

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering is immensely proud to announce a landmark achievement in the academic journey of our institution. In a remarkable display of interdisciplinary excellence, 22 students hailing from various engineering streams have successfully completed the rigorous IUCEE–NEP certification course on Quantum Computing. This specialized program, conducted in collaboration with IBM Qiskit and facilitated through the Center for Engineering Education Development (CEED), represents a bridge between classical computing paradigms and the futuristic potential of quantum mechanics. As the world stands on the precipice of a new technological era, our students have positioned themselves at the forefront by mastering the foundations of an emerging frontier that promises to redefine how we process complex information.

This success is particularly significant as it marks the inaugural cohort from our institution to receive formal, hands-on exposure to Quantum Computing. In a field where the learning curve is notoriously steep—requiring a deep understanding of linear algebra, probability, and quantum gates—these students have demonstrated exceptional intellectual curiosity and technical proficiency. By utilizing the IBM Qiskit framework, they have moved beyond theoretical concepts to engage with real-world quantum programming, gaining insights into qubits, superposition, and entanglement. This initiative aligns perfectly with the National Education Policy (NEP) goals of fostering multi-disciplinary research and equipping the next generation of engineers with "future-ready" skills that transcend traditional departmental boundaries.

The Department extends its deepest gratitude to the Heads of various Departments, the Principal, and the Director for their visionary leadership. Their unwavering support and constant encouragement have been the driving force behind creating an environment that prioritizes beyond-classroom learning and interdisciplinary collaboration. We also wish to express our heartfelt appreciation to Ms. Lakshmi Bhavani (CEED/ECE) for her dedicated mentorship. Her instrumental role in guiding the students through the intricacies of the course was vital to this high success rate. This milestone not only enhances the academic profile of our students but also strengthens our institution's reputation as a hub for cutting-edge technological education. By embracing such advanced domains, we are fostering a culture of innovation that encourages students to look beyond the horizon of conventional software development and explore the limitless possibilities of the quantum world.

Membership Drive

Sep 2, 2025 | CSE

On September 1, 2025, the Blockchain Club launched a dynamic and highly successful Membership Drive across the college campus, specifically designed to welcome the incoming batch of first-year students into the world of decentralized technology. The primary objective of this initiative was to demystify blockchain, moving it beyond the niche of cryptocurrency and presenting it as a foundational shift in how global data is managed. By emphasizing the core pillars of decentralization, security, and transparency, the club successfully raised awareness about the technology's vast real-world applications—ranging from secure voting systems to transparent supply chains. The drive was structured not just as a recruitment event, but as a strategic gateway for students to access high-value workshops, expert-led seminars, and hands-on collaborative projects that will define their technical portfolios over the next four years.

To make the learning process engaging and accessible, the club moved away from traditional lecture-based promotion and instead utilized a gamified approach: a QR code–based treasure hunt. This innovative activity required students to navigate the campus to locate various stations, each featuring a unique QR code that, when scanned, revealed fascinating technical facts about blockchain concepts. For example, a student might find a code that explains how a peer-to-peer (P2P) network eliminates the need for a central authority, or how cryptographic hashing ensures that data remains immutable and tamper-proof. This "learn-as-you-play" model proved exceptionally effective, as it transformed complex abstract ideas into a tangible, fun experience, fostering an environment of curiosity and excitement.

The response to the drive was overwhelmingly positive, resulting in a significant surge in student participation and a notable strengthening of the club’s internal community. By successfully blending entertainment with technical education, the initiative laid a robust foundation for future specialized training sessions and hackathons. It essentially served as a cultural "onboarding" for the new cohort, ensuring that they see the Blockchain Club not just as an extracurricular activity, but as a vital hub for innovation-driven learning. The drive concluded with a clear sense of momentum, positioning the club as a leader in student-led technical excellence and setting a high standard for future collaborative activities within the Department of Computer Science Engineering

3-Day Workshop On “Programming With Solidity

Nov 20, 2025 | CSE

From November 14 to November 17, 2025, the Blockchain Club, in collaboration with the Department of Computer Science Engineering, hosted a comprehensive 4-day technical workshop titled “Programming with Solidity.” Held at venues F-219 and F-220 from 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM, the intensive program was designed to transition students from theoretical understanding to practical execution within the Web3 ecosystem. The workshop began with a solid grounding in blockchain fundamentals, ensuring that all participants understood the decentralized architecture required to support programmable money. By establishing this baseline, the organizers created a clear pathway for students to grasp why smart contracts are essential for trustless digital agreements.

The core of the workshop focused on the technical mastery of Solidity, the primary programming language for the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM). Students were guided through complex topics including Solidity syntax, state variables, functions, and inheritance structures. A significant highlight was the hands-on component where participants used the Remix IDE to write, compile, and deploy their own smart contracts in a simulated environment. This practical approach allowed students to see their code interact with the blockchain in real-time. By exploring high-growth sectors like Decentralized Finance (DeFi) and Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs), the workshop successfully demonstrated the real-world utility of these skills, preparing students to innovate in the rapidly evolving landscape of decentralized applications (dApps).

A Career Guidance Session

Aug 14, 2025 | CSE

On August 13, 2025, a comprehensive Career Guidance Session was conducted for second, third, and fourth-year B.Tech students to help them navigate the increasingly complex professional landscape. The session was led by Mr. Ramesh Masuna, a Senior Faculty member at the prestigious ACE Engineering Academy, who brought a wealth of expertise in academic mentoring and competitive exam strategy. The primary objective of this seminar was to provide students with a structured roadmap for their post-graduation journey, ensuring they possess the necessary clarity to make informed decisions about their academic and professional futures. Mr. Masuna’s discourse was particularly timely for the senior cohorts, who are at a critical juncture where choosing between immediate employment, domestic higher studies, or international specialization can define their long-term career trajectory.

A central theme of the session was the strategic importance of the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE). Mr. Masuna detailed how a strong GATE score serves as a versatile tool, opening doors to advanced degrees (M.Tech/Ph.D.) at premier institutes like the IITs and IISc, while simultaneously acting as a qualifying criterion for high-paying roles in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs). He provided students with actionable preparation techniques, emphasizing consistent practice and conceptual depth. Beyond domestic opportunities, the session delved into the nuances of foreign education, covering the requirements for global examinations such as the GRE and TOEFL, and the procedural aspects of applying to international universities.

By addressing diverse career pathways—ranging from research and development to corporate leadership—the session empowered students to align their current academic planning with their ultimate professional goals. The interaction concluded with a focus on long-term goal setting, urging students to leverage their final years of engineering to build a robust technical foundation that transcends the classroom.

AI & Robotics Workshop

Aug 2, 2025 | CSE

A group of 3rd-year students participated in a two-day Artificial Intelligence & Robotics Workshop held on 31 July and 1 August 2025, organized by Ascend Initiatives in collaboration with Innow8. The workshop provided hands-on exposure to emerging technologies, real-world applications, and practical learning in AI and robotics, encouraging students to explore innovative solutions for the future.Participating in an AI and robotics workshop in 2026 is an immersive experience that bridges the gap between theoretical algorithms and physical execution. These workshops typically follow a "high-intensity, structured" model designed to turn beginners into creators within a short timeframe, often culminating in the development of a "portfolio-ready" project. As a participant, you can expect to engage in hands-on activities such as assembling robot chassis, selecting motors for specific torque-versus-speed requirements, and wiring sensor-based navigation systems. The AI component usually focuses on Edge AI and Machine Learning, where you will learn to create datasets and train models for real-time inference, such as enabling a robot to distinguish between objects or navigate a complex obstacle course autonomously.

Beyond the technical skills of coding in Python or C++ and mastering the Robot Operating System (ROS), participation offers significant professional and academic advantages. In today’s competitive landscape, admissions officers and employers prioritize "mentor-validated, deployable projects" over simple online tutorials. These workshops often emphasize Responsible AI, teaching you to document system limitations and safety thresholds through "model cards." By working in small cohorts, you also develop essential "soft" skills like collaborative debugging and technical problem framing. Whether the goal is to enter a national competition at a premier institute or to build a social-impact tool like an AI-powered healthcare assistant, these workshops provide the physical hardware and expert mentorship necessary to move from static code to dynamic, real-world motion
