A Workshop on “Full Stack Web Development”

Feb 21, 2025 | CSE-DS

On February 21, 2025, the Data Science Club and the Department of Computer Science and Engineering - Data Science (CSD) at KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology held a one- day workshop on Full Stack Web Development for 63 students from III-CSE-Data Science. The workshop was led by Mr. A.S. Arun Kumar, a developer and team lead at Levitica Technologies, Hyderabad. The workshop's goal was to teach students how to build responsive and interactive web interfaces using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, as well as server-side programming with Node.js, Express.js, and Django. It also covered databases like MySQL and MongoDB and the deployment of applications using platforms like AWS, Firebase, or Vercel

The workshop began with an introduction to web development and HTML, followed by explanations of JavaScript and CSS for front-end development. The resource person also discussed back-end development using server-side languages such as Python and Node.js frameworks. Other topics included Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) for connecting Java applications to relational databases and an introduction to GitHub for version control and collaboration After the lecture sessions, students participated in a hands-on session where they individually installed the necessary software and developed applications like registration forms. The resource person and his team clarified students' doubts during this time. The workshop concluded with a question-and-answer session and a vote of thanks from the Head of the Department, Mr. L. Govardhan, and Mr. Bande Ganesh

Impact on the students:

The workshop had a significant impact on the participating students, equipping them with practical skills and knowledge to become job-ready in the field of web development. Through hands-on projects, students gained real-world experience and the ability to build dynamic web applications from scratch. They learned to design, implement, and optimize relational and non-relational databases and how to build secure and scalable APIs for web applications. The workshop also provided students with experience in deploying web applications to production environments efficiently. Furthermore, the introduction to GitHub and its features taught them about version control, which is essential for collaborative software development. One student, Pavan Sai, even used GitHub to save his skill development code and share it with friends, demonstrating the immediate application of the learned concepts

Hackstorm 2025, a premier hackathon organized by the AIML Department, aimed to bring together innovative minds to tackle real-world challenges using artificial intelligence and machine learning. That's awesome! It sounds like the team of Ayesha Begum, Asfia Kousar, Sai Kiran, Harish, and Nagarjuna really stood out at Hackstorm 2025. Winning the first prize is a huge accomplishment, especially at such a prestigious event in AI and ML. It must have been an exciting experience for them!

The hackathon spanned and consisted of the following phases:

1. Inauguration & Keynote Speech: Experts from academia and industry shared insights on AI/ML trends.

. Problem Statement Release: Participants were given real-world challenges related to AI and ML.

3. Development Phase: Teams worked on their solutions with mentor guidance.

4. Evaluation & Presentation: Solutions were judged based on innovation, feasibility, and impact.

5. Award Ceremony & Conclusion:Winners were announced, and closing remarks were delivered.

Hackstorm 2025 successfully encouraged innovation and AI-driven problem-solving among participants. The event highlighted the growing potential of AI/ML in various domains and provided a valuable learning experience. The AIML Department looks forward to organizing future editions with even greater impact.

A Guest Lecture and Hands on session on “Big Data Analytics”

Mar 30, 2025 | CSE-DS

A guest lecture was conducted on Big Data Analytics; Dr. Praveen Kumar Yechuri, Assistant professor & manager-training & Placements, VJIT and Dr. A. Swarna, Assistant Professor, VJIT was the resource persons. The students gained insights into Big Data concepts, characteristics and its significance in various industries. Students understood how Big Data works with cloud platforms, including SAAS,PAAS and IAAS models and Hands-on experience with Hadoop tools like pig, HBase and Cassandra for real-world data Analysis. The session provided valuable insights into industry trends, carrer opportonities and essential skills in Big data Analysis.

WORLD DATA SCIENCE DAY was conducted on 13th March.2025

The objective of Data Science Day was to create an interactive platform where students could explore and deepen their understanding of data science concepts. The event aimed to enhance problem-solving, analytical, and debugging skills through engaging activities and competitions. It also sought to provide real-world insights into the applications of data science and highlight the career opportunities within the field. By incorporating hands-on learning through events like Data Charades, the Quiz, and the Debugging Challenge, the day encouraged active participation and skill development. Additionally, it aimed to foster connections between students and industry professionals through expert talks and networking opportunities

Data Charades, Connections, the Quiz Competition, and the Debugging Challenge.

In the Data Charades activity, 11 teams participated in a game where they had to guess data science-related words from clues. Each round lasted 10 minutes, and the objective was to help students become more familiar with data science concepts in a fun way. The team with the most correct guesses was declared the winner

Another team-based event,

Connections, also involved 11 teams. Participants were shown images related to data science on a projector and had to identify the connection between them. The goal of this activity was to enhance students' ability to link different data science technologies and applications. The team that identified the most correct connections won the event.For individual participants, the event offered the Quiz Competition and the Debugging Challenge.The Quiz Competition consisted of multiple-choice and short-answer questions that covered a range of topics including data science, AI, and Python. This quiz was designed to test students' theoretical and practical understanding of these concepts. The person with the highest number of correct answers was the winnerThe Debugging Challenge was another individual event that presented participants with 10 coding- related debugging questions. The primary goal was to improve students' problem-solving and debugging skills in programming. The individual who solved the most errors correctly won the challenge.

The events were a huge success, with active participation from students in all activities. The guest speech by Abhishek Mehta, an industry expert, also provided students with valuable career guidance and insights into the real-world applications of data science. Finally, trophies and certificates were presented to the winners of each event, as well as a special recognition for the overall top scorer.

Event Highlights:

Student Engagement: Active participation from students in all activities.

Industry Insights: The guest speech provided career guidance and real-world applications of data science.

Practical Learning: Hands-on exposure to problem-solving and debugging in coding competitions

Winners Recognized for Each Event:

Data Charades – Winning Team
Connections – Winning Team
Quiz Competition – Top Scorer
Debugging Challenge – Top Scorer
Trophies and Certificates: Presented by Chief Guest Abhishek Mehta, Daneal Sir, HoD, and the Club President.
Special Recognition for the Overall Top Scorer of the Event.

Closing Ceremony & Vote of Thanks:

Closing Speech by Faculty Coordinator: Expressing gratitude to all participants and guests.
Thanking the Organizers & Volunteers for making the event a success.
Encouragement for Future Participation in data science workshops and club activities.

Civil KGRCET Team “RedRock” Wins Rs. 50,000 Funding in i2I Challenge 2024-25

Mar 31, 2025 | Civil

We are thrilled to announce that Team RedRock from KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology has secured Rs. 50,000 in funding for their groundbreaking project in the Ideas to Impact Challenge (i2I) 2024-25. Their innovative research focuses on developing a sustainable, carbon-negative building material, which aligns with global sustainability goals and contributes to environmentally friendly construction solutions.

The team, led by Chakali Government (4th Year, Civil Engineering) and supported by team members Kurimilla Vivek (4th Year), Mohammed Khadar Baba (3rd Year), and Bhukya Dhanalaxmi (3rd Year), is working towards optimizing and implementing their "RedRock" material. Their project has been guided by Dr. V. Srinivasa Reddy, Professor of Civil Engineering, who provided strategic and technical mentorship.

With application number i2I2024M0085, the team’s success in the competition highlights the innovation and research excellence fostered at KGRCET. This funding will support the next phase of their research and development, bringing them closer to real-world applications of their sustainable building material.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Dr. Srinivasa Reddy and Team RedRock for this remarkable achievement. We look forward to seeing their project make a significant impact in the field of sustainable construction!

2. Student-Parent Meeting on Attendance and Counselling – Civil Engineering Department

The Department of Civil Engineering organized a Student-Parent Meeting to address the issue of attendance shortage among students. The meeting was conducted under the guidance of Dr. Soumya Sucharita Singha, Associate Professor and Head of the Department, and was attended by concerned students along with their parents.

During the session, Dr. Soumya Sucharita Singha emphasized the importance of regular attendance, academic discipline, and consistent engagement in academic activities. Detailed insights into each student’s attendance and performance were shared, and the underlying causes for absenteeism were discussed constructively.

The department also arranged counseling support for students, focusing on improving time management, motivation, and goal orientation. Parents were encouraged to play an active role in their ward’s academic progress and personal development.

This proactive initiative underscores the department’s commitment to nurturing responsible, well-rounded students through continuous support and collaboration with parents.

A Guest Lecture on “Operating System:

May 3, 2025 | CSE-DS

A guest lecture on "Operating System" was organized by the Department of Computer Science & Engineering - Data Science (CSD) for second-year students on May 3, 2025, at KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology. The event, which was attended by 61 students, was designed to introduce them to operating system concepts, including CPU scheduling, deadlock, and the design and development of operating systems.

The guest speaker was Mr. Kottu Santosh Kumar, an Assistant Professor from the Department of IT at Vardhaman College of Engineering, Hyderabad Mr.Kottu            Santosh            Kumar,Assistant Professor,Dept.of IT, Vardhaman College of Engineering, Hyderabad,,has been invited for the One Day Workshop. The session started with addressing the participants and introduction of the guest by Dr.Srinivas Jhade, Associate Professor, Computer Science and Engineering- Data Science.

The guest lecture on Operating Systems served as a valuable platform for students to deepen their understanding of fundamental concepts and their real-world applications. It was a well-structured session, starting from basic introductions and progressing to more specific topics like file system management and system calls. The event successfully met its objectives, preparing students to better understand the intricacies of operating systems and their role in computing

Impact on the students:

The guest lecture on Operating Systems had a notable impact on the students by providing them with a deeper understanding of fundamental concepts and their practical applications. Students were equipped with the ability to manage access to a computer and its files, demonstrating a solid grasp of core operating system functions. The session also enhanced their problem-solving skills, as a key outcome was the ability to "recognize and resolve user problems with standard operating environments".

Furthermore, the lecture provided valuable practical knowledge regarding the interaction between programming languages, operating systems, and computer architectures. This practical focus was particularly evident in the detailed discussion on File System Interface and Operations. The students were taught about various access methods, directory structures, protection, and allocation methods

A Guest Lecture on “Search Engine Optimization and Web Analytics” was conducted on 03rd May 2024

May 3, 2025 | CSE-DS

A seminar on "Search Engine Optimization and Web Analytics" was held on May 3, 2025, at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology, organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering-Data Science in collaboration with the Department of Master of Business Administration. The seminar was attended by 57 students from both III-Year CSE-Data Science and I MBA. The objective was to provide a comprehensive overview of key concepts, tools, and techniques for web analytics, SEO, and digital marketing

The seminar's resource person was Mr. Narsingh Patro,a     Senior              Area    Head   at                 Housing.Com, Hyderabad. The session was introduced by Dr. Sarika Koluguri from the Department of MBA and Mr. Bande Ganesh from the Department of CSE-Data Science. Mr. Patro covered various topics, including the fundamentals of SEO and its importance in digital marketing. He also discussed keyword planning tools like Google Keyword Planner and Ubersuggest , as well as the SEO lifecycle. Technical aspects such as Schema Markup, Structured Data, Site Speed, Core Web Vitals, and Mobile-First Indexing were also explained  with     real-time  examples     and  sample programs. The seminar also delved intoWeb Analytics and Data Analyticsincluding traffic analysis and understanding key terminologies and data types. The use ofGoogle Search Console for performance reports and mobile usability was also covered. Following the lecture, Mr. Patro conducted group activities focused on using analytics for business improvement.

Impact on the students:

The seminar had a significant impact on students, equipping them with both theoretical knowledge and hands-on experience. Participants gained a clear understanding of how search engines work and the importance of SEO in digital marketing. They learned to conduct

keyword research and develop effective SEO content strategies. A key outcome was the ability to use web analytics tools to track and interpret website performance data. This enabled them to create detailed SEO and analytics reports for performance improvement and decision-making. Students also gained knowledge of digital marketing concepts. The hands-on activities on

keyword research and keyword planning tools were particularly impactful, fostering collaborative learning and practical application of the concepts discussed. The students were also introduced to technical aspects of website optimization for better crawlability and indexing. The seminar successfully provided a blend of theoretical knowledge and practical skills, preparing the students for careers in digital marketing and data-driven roles

Guest Lecture on “The Role of Supplementary Cementitious Materials in Sustainable Concrete”

May 15, 2025 | Civil

The Department of Civil Engineering, KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology, organized an insightful online guest lecture titled "The Role of Supplementary Cementitious Materials in Sustainable Concrete" on 3rd May 2025 for II-Year, II-Semester B.Tech students.

The session was delivered by Dr. Srikanth Koniki, Assistant Professor, Department of Civil Engineering, CBIT, Hyderabad. Dr. Koniki shared his expertise on the importance of using supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) such as fly ash, slag, silica fume, and metakaolin to improve the durability and sustainability of concrete. His presentation emphasized how SCMs contribute to reducing the carbon footprint of construction activities while enhancing the performance of concrete in various structural applications.

A total of 32 students actively participated in the session, gaining valuable knowledge on sustainable practices in civil engineering.

Mrs. P. Rajitha and Mr. K. Sai Kumar Chary, Assistant Professors from the Department of Civil Engineering, coordinated the session. Their efforts in organizing this session contributed to the students' academic enrichment and understanding of eco-friendly construction materials.

A Guest Lecture on “Big data Analytics ” was conducted on 15th May 2025

May 16, 2025 | CSE-DS

A guest lecture on "Big Data Analytics" was organized by the Data Science Club in collaboration with the Department of Computer Science & Engineering - Data Science (CSD) at KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology on May 15, 2025. The one-day event was held for III-CSE-Data Science students and saw the participation of 63 students. The objective was to provide           students with        knowledge             of            machine                learning, recommendation systems, and mobile and social media analytics The guest lecturer, Dr. Mathurya, an Assistant Professor from Vardhaman College of Engineering, Hyderabad, is a specialist in Data Analytics and Machine Learning. The session began with an introduction of the guest by the session coordinator, Mrs. K. Gomathi,                               Assistant                Professor,              Computer              Science  and Engineering-Data Science. Dr. Mathurya initiated the lecture with an introduction to Big Data Analytics. The topics discussed included an introduction to Data Analytics, Machine Learning, and social media analytics. She also explained the categories of supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, as well as recommendation systems and collaborative filtering. The lecture provided a detailed explanation of mobile analytics, social media analytics, and BigR.

Impact on the students:

The guest lecture had a significant impact on the students, as highlighted by the hands-on session that followed the theoretical talk. Students gained practical experience by implementing different types of supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms using R/Python. This hands- on experience allowed them to build a machine learning model from scratch using a given dataset. They also learned to design models using supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning algorithms. The students were able to develop applications for customer and mobile analytics , as well as applications for social media analytics. Dr. Mathurya clarified their doubts while they were developing their models and applications. One of the notable impacts was the introduction to RStudio and its features, as well as the use of GitHub

In his address, Mr. Damodar provided a practical overview of current industry trends, expectations from fresh graduates, and the evolving skill sets required to succeed in today’s competitive job market. He emphasized the importance of continuous learning, soft skills, adaptability, and domain-specific technical expertise.

The session also offered guidance on resume building, interview preparation, and strategies for aligning academic pursuits with career goals. Students interacted enthusiastically, posing questions and gaining clarity on real-world challenges faced in the corporate environment.

5. Mr .Bharath Naik ,M.Ravi kumar and R.Dinesh Kumar  Completes Internship at Defence Electronics Research Laboratory (DLRL), Hyderabad .

The  student of Mechanical Engineering at  KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology, has successfully completed a project internship at the DLRL Hyderabad, a premier unit under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India.

The internship, held from 5th May to 30th May 2025, focused on the project titled “CNC Machining.” During this period, The above students engaged in practical applications and technical learning, contributing to a key research area under the guidance of experienced scientists at DLRL.

The certificate of completion acknowledges that his work met the requirements and expectations of the laboratory and that he satisfactorily fulfilled the assigned tasks. The project serves as a part of the partial fulfillment of his B.Tech Degree in Mechanical Engineering.

6. On 12th May 2025, The Department of Mechanical Engineering at KG Reddy College of Engineering & Technology (KGRCET) successfully organized an insightful guest lecture on the topic "Introduction to Governing Equations of Fluid in CFD". The session took place in Room F-201 from 10:30 AM to 1:00 PM.

The guest speaker for the event was Mr. Manish Vyas, COCO L2 – Manager at UPGRAD Education Pvt. Ltd., who brought with him valuable industry knowledge and experience in Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). His talk focused on the core governing equations of fluid flow and their application in CFD simulations, a vital area for aspiring mechanical engineers and researchers in fluid mechanics.

The session aimed at bridging the gap between academic theory and industrial applications, giving students a solid foundation in the mathematical and physical principles behind CFD tools.

The lecture was coordinated by Ms. Gangavarapu Tanya Psalms, Assistant Professor, who ensured smooth execution of the event and encouraged student interaction throughout the session

7. Dr. Udaya Sri Kakarla Participates in National Webinar on Intellectual Property Rights & Commercialization.Dr. Udaya Sri Kakarla has been officially recognized for participating in a national-level webinar on "Intellectual Property Rights & Commercialization", conducted by the National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme) - Ministry of MSME, Government of India on 30th April 2025 .

Inauguration of SAEINDIA Collegiate Club at KG Reddy College:

Jun 30, 2025 | Mech

1.Faculty Members Completed  AICTE FDP on Sustainable Additive Manufacturing

Mr.S.Sathish ,Mr.K.Anil and Mr. Bhonagiri Ramesh, Assistant Professor at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology, Moinabad, Hyderabad, successfully completed a Faculty Development Program (FDP) organized by the AICTE Training and Learning (ATAL) Academy. The program, titled "Sustainable Additive Manufacturing in Medical Applications: UN SDG Perspectives", was hosted by Lords Institute of Engineering and Technology from June 15 to June 20, 2025.

2.Inauguration of SAEINDIA Collegiate Club at KG Reddy College

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology hosted the inaugural ceremony of the SAEINDIA Collegiate Club on June 19, 2025. The event took place at the Seminar Hall, KGR College, beginning at 11:30 AM. Mr. Ramesha BS, Head – Academic Initiatives at Altair India inaugurated the Club along with Dr.Rohit kandakatla,Dr.M.N.Narsaiah ,Dr.L.Jayahari and Head of the event  Mrs.K.Kalpan .

This newly established club, affiliated with SAEINDIA (Society of Automotive Engineers India), aims to promote innovation, technical excellence, and industry-relevant skills among engineering students. The initiative marks a significant step toward strengthening automotive and mechanical engineering engagement

3. The Faculty Members of Mechanical Department have Attend Workshop on Outcome-Based Education at KG Reddy College

On June 21, 2025, the Centre for Engineering Education Development (CEED), in association with the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC), organized a one-day workshop on “Engineering Program Outcomes in Focus: Writing Competencies and Performance Indicators for Outcome-Based Education (OBE)” at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology.

Dr. Vijayalakshmi M., Professor at KLE Technological University, served as the resource person for the workshop, which focused on enhancing faculty skills in designing and evaluating program outcomes.

Mrs.K. Kalpana, Head of the Mechanical Engineering Department and Faculty members have actively participated in the session, reaffirming the institution’s commitment to continuous improvement in academic quality and educational practices.

4.A Seminar on “Power of Optimization for Smart Product Development” at KGRCET organized by Department of Mechanical Engineering inassociation with SAE-collegiate club KGRCET

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology organized an insightful seminar on "Power of Optimization for Smart Product Development" on 19th June 2025. The session, held in the Seminar Hall, was conducted in collaboration with SAEINDIA.

The keynote speaker for the event was Mr. Ramesha BS, Head – Academic Initiatives at Altair India. With his vast industry experience, Mr. Ramesha enlightened students and faculty on the role of optimization in engineering design and how it leads to smarter, more efficient product development.

The seminar emphasized the importance of modern simulation tools, design thinking, and innovation in today's competitive engineering landscape. It was an engaging and enriching experience for all attendees, bridging the gap between academic learning and industrial application.

The Head of the department  Mrs.K.Kalpana  extends its gratitude to Mr. Ramesha and SAEINDIA for making this seminar a great success.

5. Mechanical Department Holds PRC Meeting on SDG-Linked Projects

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology conducted a Project Review Committee (PRC) meeting on June 28, 2025, at 9:00 AM. The agenda included PRC team work allocation, reviewing the status of student project problem statements, and exploring their alignment with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

The meeting, chaired by the PRC Chairperson-Mrs K.Kalpana  and coordinated by the Dr.D.Baloji PRC coordinator , aimed to streamline project evaluation and strengthen the relevance of academic work to global challenges. All faculty members and project guides actively participated in the session.

6.The faculty members from Mechanical department attended the Workshop on Publishing in High Impact Journals Held at KG Reddy College

The Centre for Research Innovation and Development (CRID) at KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology organized a workshop on "Writing and Publishing Research Articles in High Impact Journals" on June 17, 2025.

The session was conducted by Prof. Kunal Gaurav from the School of Business, MIT World Peace University, Pune. Held from 1:30 PM to 3:30 PM in the Seminar Hall, the event was attended by Deans, HoDs, and faculty members, particularly Ph.D. pursuing scholars.

The initiative aimed to enhance research writing skills and improve publication success in reputed journals.

Three-day hands-on workshop titled “IoT Skill-a-Thon”, for III and IV ECE students,

Oct 24, 2025 | ECE

The Department of ECE in association with IoT club organized a three-day hands-on workshop titled “IoT Skill-a-Thon”, for III and IV ECE students, aimed at enhancing students’ practical knowledge and skills in the Internet of Things (IoT).

During the workshop, participants explored the fundamentals of Raspberry Pi, Python programming, and the working principles of various sensors and actuators. Students gained practical exposure by interfacing sensors and actuators with Raspberry Pi to identify and monitor different environmental parameters from their surroundings. They also developed mini IoT-based applications, integrating the acquired knowledge into real-time use cases.

On the third day, students showcased their projects through presentations and demonstrations, highlighting their learning outcomes and innovative approaches. A total of 11 teams participated, out of which two teams were recognized as Best Performers for their outstanding creativity and technical execution.

Guest Lecture on “PID to state space designing efficient Feed back Control systems”

Nov 15, 2025 | ECE

The guest lecture on “PID to State Space: Designing Efficient Feedback Control Systems” provided III B.Tech ECE students with a comprehensive overview of control system fundamentals, covering system modeling, block diagram reduction, and feedback principles. It emphasized time-domain and frequency-domain analyses using tools such as Routh–Hurwitz, Bode, Nyquist, and Root Locus plots to evaluate stability and performance. The session also explained PID controllers and lead–lag compensators, linking theoretical concepts to real-world engineering applications. Overall, the lecture enhanced students’ conceptual clarity, practical understanding, and interest in control engineering.

Resource Person:

Ms. S. Swetha

Assistant Professor, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering ,MGIT College

Guest Lecture on Applications of IOT

Jun 21, 2022 | CSE

Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering organised a Guest lecture on IoT apphcations to III CSE students on 21-06-2022. The coordinator of the program Mr. Vijaya Bhasker reddy introduced speaker Mr. Basava Dhanne to all the students and handed over the session to speaker. The main obejctive of this program is to create awareness on IoT applications and their implementation in current societal needs. Where students can develop their own IoT projects relavent to different applications The speaker stered the session with an introduction to the IoT, definition and current stauts of IoT across the world. Also gave detailed information about various hardware modules used like Contorl units like ARDUINO, ESP8266 and Raspberrypi etc, Sensors and Actuators like DHTII, DHT22, Gas sensor LCD display, Buzzer etc, also discussed about various software The history of IoT and the Frequency bands used also presented for students. The term 'Internet of Things' was coined in 1999 by the computer scientist Kevin Ashton. While working at Procter & Gamble, Ashton proposed putting radio-frequency identification (RFID) chips on products to track them through a supply chain. tools used like ARDUINO IDE, programming languages as Python, Java etc A novel IoT application like Garbage Monitoring System is shown and explained in detail, how IoT make use of this in daily life. a waste management system introduced here in which each dumpster is embedded in a monitoring system that will notify the corresponding personal if the dumpster is full. In this system, it is also possible to separate wet and dry waste into two separate containers. This system provides an effective solution to the waste management problem

Guest Lecture on “Soil Investigation for Civil Engineering Structures”

Dec 7, 2022 | Civil

Department of Civil Engineering has organized a guest lecture on the topic “Soil Investigation for Civil Engineering Structures” on 07th December 2022 for our final year and third year students of the Department of Civil Engineering, KGRCET in offline mode. The eminent expert Mr. Nafees Ahmed (Retired Executive Engineer), Irrigation & CAD Department, Telangana had been invited to deliver the lecture. The speaker explained about the basics of soil investigation and what are the tests need to be carried out at the site before construction. He also took case studies to make student understand the concepts and all the students understood the borehole data how to be read. He explained soil investigation consists of two stages, such as firstly, Preliminary investigation. Reconnaissance survey which involves study of topography, excavations, drainage pattern, streams etc. Secondly, Detailed investigation which is carried out to study the nature, sequence and extent of subsoil strata and location of ground water table. During detailed investigation, disturbed and undisturbed samples are collected from different locations and from different depths by boring. After explaining, he interacted and asked few questions to students and almost all the questions were answered by the students. After the interaction, he then further continued his lecture where he explained about the field tests carried out with few case studies.

Jul 30, 2022 | CSE

IMPACT ANALYSIS

Based on the attainments for the batch 2017-2021 on Formal Language Automata Theory of the A.Y. 2020-2021 II-II SEM, the course was initiated to stream of CSE-AI & ML. Also, based on the feedback of the students and some teachers, the gap has been identified. So, to fulfill it, we have organized the Guest Lecture for the A.Y. 2021-2022.

The resource person Dr. Rambabu Pemula, Associate Professor, with over 14+ years of Teaching & Research in Dept. of CSE, Raghu Engineering College (Autonomous), Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.

The content organized based on the inputs provided by the students in a sequence manner.

The speaker has discussed about the main objective of this program is to create awareness on Context-Free Grammar and Turing Machines and their utilization in current research and societal needs. The speaker steered the session with an introduction to the Chomsky’s hierarchy and grammar with comparison. Also gave detailed information about various types of grammars syntax with examples.

Students performed and learned well in the theory and also students completed solving the problems which were given by the faculty members. After attending the session, the students gained knowledge on some key important features. Based on their knowledge and skill, the students were helped led to asymptotic complexity as a way to compare performance of algorithms. Another major advance was that the Turing model led to the notion of an instantaneous description of a computation and a valid computation.

Summary Report

Event Overview

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering organised a Guest lecture on Context-Free Grammar and Turing Machines for II CSE-AIML students on 30-07-2022. The coordinator of the program, Dr. Harikrishna Bommala, introduced the speaker, Dr. Rambabu Pemula, to all the students and handed over the session to the speaker.

Objectives

The main objective of this program is to create awareness on Context-Free Grammar and Turing Machines and their utilization in current research and societal needs.

Key Topics Covered

The speaker steered the session with an introduction to the Chomsky’s hierarchy and grammar with comparison. He also gave detailed information about various types of grammars syntax with examples.

Chomsky’s Hierarchy: Includes Type 0, Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3. The session discussed various grammars with their specific restrictions and productions.
Context-Free Grammar (CFG): Defined as a formal grammar used to generate all possible patterns of strings in a given formal language. It consists of a set of production rules ($G$) used to generate the strings of a language.
Derivations and Parsing: * Left-most derivation: When the sentential form of an input is scanned and replaced from left to right.
Parse Tree: A hierarchical representation of terminals or non-terminals representing the derivation of the grammar to yield input strings.
Normal Forms: Discussed the term "context-free," where a non-terminal symbol ($V$) can always be replaced by a string ($w$) regardless of context.
GNF (Greibach Normal Form): A CFG is in GNF if all production rules satisfy specific conditions, such as a start symbol generating $\epsilon$ or a non-terminal generating a terminal.
Turing Machines: Described as consisting of an infinitely long tape divided into cells, each containing a 1, a 0, or an empty space. A "head" moves left or right to read the symbols written in the cells.

Conclusion

Through automata, computer scientists are able to understand how machines compute functions and solve problems. More importantly, it helps define what it means for a function to be computable or for a question to be described as decidable.

How to use this text:
Formatting: I have used bold headers and bullet points to make the report easier to read in Word.
Equations: I used LaTeX formatting for technical symbols like $G$ (Grammar) and $\epsilon$ (Epsilon) to ensure they look professional.

Summary Report:

Computer architecture is a set of rules and methods that describe the functionality, organization, and implementation of computer systems. The architecture of a system refers to its structure in terms of separately specified components of that system and their inter-relationships. The main topics of this course include Micro-programmed Control, Central Processing Unit, Data Representation, and Computer Arithmetic.

Mention down the criteria

It is important to make a list of several criteria before joining the best engineering colleges in Hyderabad. If the students have to select the between engineering colleges, then the student should go for the best college depending upon –

Several scholarships are available for students choosing up the stream of engineering. Several mechanical scholarships, civil and ECE scholarships, offered to aspirants as the financial opportunity to enhance their future.

Personal Choice:-

Reputation:-
Engineers enhance our country’s reputation with their knowledge and skills and maintain high living standards, national security, and the best well being. Must-Read Tips For Students To Enhance Efficiency In Higher Education

Aug 4, 2021 | News

Have you managed to grab admission to the top university in India? Are you happy to be a part of a top tier education institution? If your answer is in the affirmative, then it is time that you also get accustomed to the idea of making the most while you study in the prestigious college/university of any region. Getting admitted to the institution of your choice is one angle of the side and using the time constructively in such an educational society is another. Looking at the other side of the coin, it is essential to understand the ways to enhance your time spent in such educational institutions that leaves a lasting impression on your career ahead. KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology is one of the best engineering colleges in Hyderabad catering to UG and PG courses in Science and Technology.

Students who get through college should consider themselves lucky to be a part of a system that believes in holistic education. The college came into existence in the year 2008 with the perspective to create next-generation engineers. Engineering is one of the most sought-after professions in India and the campus believes in extending the best education to the students in the related stream. However, it is also important that the students develop a positive attitude to amalgamate their skills and put it to the best use.

Here are a few tips that graduate-level students can undertake to become successful in their careers:

Develop an effective study pattern

Rote learning is not recommended at all at any stage of education because it disrupts the foundation and conceptual approach of education. Students should indulge and invest their time to understand the concepts and put them to the best use. Formulating questions based on the study material and then clarifying the doubts with the respective teacher will enhance learning skills and help develop a complete understanding of the subject. Another effective way to reinforce the lesson studied is to quiz oneself. This will help to review the chapters and understand the logic conveyed by the lesson in an impactful manner.

Don’t skip lectures

While one of the most exciting parts of attending college or university can be to fall easy prey to missing classes; it is not recommended for engineering students at all. The missing lecture may mean missing an important part of the chapter that can disrupt your understanding of the chapter.

Making notes

Though it may sound repetitive and an orthodox way of learning, yet it is the most useful and impactful means to ensure that learning is effective. Be attentive in the class and focus to make those small notes when the lecturer is explaining concepts. Ask questions whenever you feel that you are getting stuck with the understanding. It will help you to grab the essence of the lesson instantly.

Ask questions

Don’t feel intimidated to ask questions in between the class as well. It is the best time to clarify doubts with the teacher when the concept teaching is in progress. If it is not possible to ask the questions in the class, then make sure to clarify the doubts once the class is over. Such a study habit and pattern will help you go a long way in your career too. Pitch for the extra classes offered by the professor. It is one of the best ways to communicate one-on-one with the educator to clarify the doubts and get a better grip of the subject.

Collaborate

Always reach out to your peers because collaboration and working/studying in the team can help develop a team spirit right from the formative years. This habit will help you develop managerial skills and take your career to new heights later in the professional world. In the university, such an attitude will help you study collectively and to get involved with the student community in the institution. The top engineering college in Hyderabad gives a congenial environment to the students for proper growth and development. The relationships that you make in your engineering college will lead to great networking skills that will be of much use in your career too.

KGRCET is one of the best education institutions where students are nurtured to become future leaders. The campus is equipped with all the modern amenities that aids in better studying and the growth prospects of the students is bright. The institution is equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure and a proficient team of educators.

How To Select The Best Engineering College In Hyderabad? Find The Answer In This Article.

Jul 23, 2021 | News

Graduation persuasion is the most significant part of life for every student to succeed in life. These four years decide your career and your professional position in your life. There are many small and large engineering institutions established in the past years. So, choosing the right college for pursuing your graduation could be the most difficult task for both parents and students. 

You often question yourself like ‘Which college is best, ‘What course should I choose?’, ‘How to choose the right career. So, in this article, you can find your answer on choosing the right engineering college. Here are some of the factors that are to be considered to choose the best engineering college. 

Location:-

Location is one of the vital things that are to be considered when choosing a college. Considering the admission in the college which is near to your hometown and your place would be beneficial that could save your travel time and travel cost. So, choose the college near your home or choose the best college that has a great hostel facility. And also the college place should be peaceful and away from the city. 

Choose the best engineering stream:-

Pick the engineering stream upon your interest and passion which pays the way towards your career success. So, never compromise on your interested engineering stream and go for it. Since you have chosen the right engineering branch, you will be more encouraged and interested to take on challenges in the upcoming four years. 

Categorize and consider colleges:-

While if you are categorizing your search down to colleges, ensure that you consider all the vital points such as location, cost, accreditation and engineering stream. You must also have backup colleges and engineering stream plan options so that you can adopt one of those, if in case you are unable to acquire the selected stream. You can make your categorization as - top colleges, average colleges, above-average colleges in which you have most chances of getting admissions. 

List your Criteria:-

It is always important to write down a checklist of all the vital factors which can help you to shortlist the best engineering colleges in Hyderabad. Some of the features that can be significant to notice are the travel distance, location, accreditation, degree, placement, financial help or scholarships, faculty experience, campus life, social life & campus facilities. 

Be prepared for your entrance exam:-

With the emerging competition to acquire admissions in the top-ranked colleges, it has become essential for students to take expert guidance to be prepared to qualify in several engineering institutions. Therefore, it is also important to enhance one’s core subjects such as Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics from high school to increase the score of engineering entrance examinations. 

Evaluate your priorities:-

Evaluate the pros and cons of every selected college and rank them according to the scale of 1 to 10 on different aspects such as college infrastructure, teacher & student ratio, hostel facilities, college reputation, an affiliation of university, placement record, ranking of college, recognition & more. 

Check for scholarships and financial aid:-

Look at the scholarship eligibility criteria mentioned by the engineering colleges, so that you possess multiple choices of getting into the right colleges without fees and can have a hassle-free education. 

Campus Tour:-

Before finalizing the college, make sure that you tour the colleges and observe the college environment. While you are touring college, you must especially visit laboratories, libraries and sports facilities. You can also make interactions with the students and faculty about the college to know their experience at the college. 

Experienced faculty:-

Many colleges are lacking behind for good faculty. Some colleges don’t even have the required subject faculty. Before taking admission to an engineering college, you must check the faculty of the college and their experience. Because the best faculty provide the best subject knowledge to students which help them at the time of campus placements. 

Campus Placements:-

Any college provides a 100% campus placement guarantee. But the colleges which have more connections with the many companies would be beneficial for you to have more chances of getting hired. The college should provide special training skills which would help you to crack the jobs. 

KGRCET, the top engineering college in Hyderabad provides the quality education and skills to enhance the career of every student. They provide a highly experienced faculty and great campus infrastructure which makes students' campus life memorable.

The KGR Philosophy – Engineering India’s Change Makers

Jul 28, 2021 | News

Albert Einstein once said, “Scientists investigate that which already is; engineers create that which has never been.” Engineers play a pivotal role in our society. It is they who create, design and develop the state-of-the-art, for our everyday. Bill Gates, in his book “How to Avoid a Climate Disaster” highlighted the various ways in which humans are polluting our planet earth by increasing carbon emissions in the atmosphere. He argues that the average temperature of the planet is gradually rising, and we could eventually enter a new ice age if we do not become carbon neutral in the next few decades. He asserts that the world is currently emitting 51 billion tons of greenhouse gases and we need to aim to get to Carbon Zero. He talks about the various breakthroughs we need to develop clean energy products that will have zero carbon footprint on the environment and how engineers will have the greatest role in achieving these targets.

It is therefore of utmost importance, to nurture our future engineers. Ones that aspire to rise beyond just engineering. Rise to become change-makers. With the vision, ideas, capabilities, and conviction to change the world

At KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology, we believe in empowering our engineers to become leaders in their community, where they voice their opinions for change and lead efforts that are focussed on their socio-economic development in a sustainable approach. Our philosophy is driven by the need to develop holistic well-rounded engineers who possess four important qualities – Intelligence Quotient, Innovation Quotient, Social Quotient, and Emotional Quotient. These four elements are important measures of evaluating the holistic development of students that will prepare them for becoming the leaders of tomorrow

Students at KGRCET are provided with an ecosystem designed to nurture these four elements through a strategic approach. The curriculum is inclusive of industry-relevant courses that are aimed to build the industry-academia gap and prepare our students for employment in their interest domain upon graduation. Our innovative teaching and learning culture provides students with active and experiential learning opportunities that would enable them to innovate. Students are provided with hands-on learning opportunities as they are made to work on developing technological solutions to address the problems identified in our neighbouring communities. We believe such experiences will build a student’s emotional quotient and help empathise with problems in the society. Students are provided with a range of co-curricular and extracurricular activities that will help them build their social quotient. Both emotional and social quotients are considered to be crucial for the development of leadership qualities among individuals. We recommend students to be strategic and follow a 4-year plan for their undergraduate education that includes academics, co-curricular and extracurricular activities

Within those four years at KGRCET, we work to transform our engineering students into change makers who eventually champion a sustainable approach to social and economic development. Including the fight against climate change.

Engineers must be critical yet creative; curious yet capable; as well as ready to handle the constantly changing world. The engineering portfolio knows no bounds, but these people are all working to the same common goal – building a sustainable world. Whatever you wish to contribute to society through your engineering dedication, nothing compares to impacting people’s lives, and the world for that matter, for the better.

About the Author

Dr. Rohit Kandakatla is the Director of KG Reddy College of Engineering and Technology and has completed his PhD in Engineering Education from Purdue University. His work involves building Engineering Education Ecosystems through Social Innovation, Research, Entrepreneurship, and Technology.

Research interests include education policy, community-based learning, understanding organisational development, and integration of technology and entrepreneurship in engineering education.

There is no such college as the best college, but there are many colleges that are best for you. Here are some of the guidelines that you can follow to choose the right engineering college. 

Choose an engineering stream:-

Before selecting the best engineering college, you need to first decide which engineering branch you are going to pursue. Branch selection is a vital step because students may not feel much interested in doing a course if they don’t feel motivated enough. The branch that you select decides your success and passion in life. So, take time and decide your interest stream and pave the way for your successful career.

Categorize and consider colleges:-

After deciding the engineering stream, the next step is to select the other three streams in case you are not eligible for your selected stream. It is the best decision to categorize the colleges into three groups based on priorities. The first group should contain the top engineering colleges in Hyderabad which are hard to get into. The second category comes with above-average colleges which are easy to get admission to. The third group is categorized with colleges that have very easy access to get admission. Categorizing colleges in this way is the best way to choose the right engineering college for you. 

Mention your criteria:-

Write down a list of features you want to consider and choose your right fit college. Here are some of the considerations that can be included below:

Offered degree
Location
Distance covered from home
Government or Private
Financial aid or scholarship
Cost
Campus resources
Placement and internship
Expert faculty
Accreditation
Quality/ Reputation
Student life
Social life
Past performance of college

Choosing the right course is based on the interest of the student in the specified subject and their abilities and knowledge. If the student has the choice of two engineering colleges for the same engineering stream, the better-performed college would be the best option that should be chosen. The faculty qualification and experience is one of the most significant elements that have to be considered to avail the quality education and experience. 

Rank priorities:-

Write down a list of pros and cons of the engineering colleges that you are considering and rate them according to the different factors of college such as affordability, home distance, teacher-student ratio, faculty, facilities, & college infrastructure. When you compare different factors, you can find the leading college and be confident about your final decision. Looking for scholarships and financial aid is vital and if you get any of them, you can keep the college in the top priority which you made into the second choice because you are unable to afford it.

Research opportunities and Facilities:-

The top engineering college provides the best research facilities for the aspirants. These facilities include labs with the latest technologies and also government grants. You have to look for the undertaken initiatives, check out the in-house scholars that are published and any of the awards presented to the college by the government.

Take a look at the college’s placement records from the past years, the average salary that is taken by the students who have pursued their engineering course and also have a glance at the placement partners and their reputation. Because a good placement history provides you with the best number of opportunities to enhance your career towards success.
